readings.core_relation: Position-controlled question answering and UUID retrieval distinguish accepting context from using evidence: middle-position evidence often lowers accuracy, longer windows offer little advantage on shared-length inputs, and query repetition fixes lookup without fixing question answering. Better retrieval recall also need not improve reader accuracy.
readings.scope: Evaluated models and tasks only; some GPT-3.5-Turbo document conditions underperform closed-book answers; both evaluated Claude variants retrieve UUIDs nearly perfectly.
readings.witness: distinguish input capacity from effective evidence use

readings.core_relation: Offline critic labels train the generator to predict reflection tokens; during inference, segment-level beam search combines generation probabilities with normalized relevance, support, and utility scores to select passage-conditioned sentence continuations. Evidence judgments thereby affect selection, with thresholds and weights adjustable without retraining or an inference-time critic.
readings.scope: Llama 2 critic distilled from GPT-4 annotations; retrieved passage text is loss-masked; utility is judged independently of passages.
readings.witness: its judged relationship to the response affects selection

readings.core_relation: Relocating answer-bearing paragraphs while fixing the question, document set, and answer isolates evidence-position sensitivity; changing distractor counts tests additional context. Closed-book and answer-only prompts provide baselines, while UUID lookup reduces linguistic confounders.
readings.scope: 2,655 NaturalQuestions-Open queries; 10, 20, or 30 documents; 75, 140, or 300 UUID pairs with 500 examples per setting; greedy decoding and output-inclusion scoring.
readings.witness: Reordering tests position at a fixed length

readings.core_relation: With identical five-passage inputs, SELF-RAG 7B greatly improves ASQA citation precision and recall over Llama2-FT 7B but slightly lowers correctness. The ablation favors the combined configuration; stronger support weighting costs MAUVE fluency, and reduced retrieval harms PopQA more than PubHealth.
readings.scope: Citation precision/recall: 66.9%/67.8% versus 5.0%/7.5%; str-em: 30.0 versus 31.0. Ablation: 50,000 training examples, 150 ASQA questions; passage handling and reflection supervision both change.
readings.witness: not interchangeable improvements in overall answer quality
readings.unclear: Critique tokens' isolated effect is not recoverable.

readings.core_relation: Self-RAG learns retrieval decisions and evidence judgments as reflection tokens, then uses their probabilities to rank passage-conditioned sentences without a separate inference-time critic. This enables adjustable evidence-aware generation, but improved attribution does not ensure coverage or fluency.
readings.scope: Zero-shot 7B/13B evaluation on six tasks; PopQA improves over a same-data baseline. ASQA 13B precision is 70.3 versus 65.1, recall 71.3 versus 76.6; 7B support weighting trades precision for MAUVE.
readings.witness: allow behavior to change without retraining

readings.core_relation: Repeating queries fixes synthetic lookup but leaves question-answering positional weaknesses; supplied answer evidence among distractors can perform worse than no documents. Beyond 20 retrieved documents, reader gains remain marginal despite rising recall, separating lookup and retrieval success from effective answering.
readings.scope: GPT-3.5-Turbo (16K), 300 UUID pairs: 100% with repetition versus 45.6% worst-position accuracy without it. Some 20/30-document GPT-3.5-Turbo settings fall below the 56.1% closed-book baseline.
readings.witness: does not provide a general remedy

readings.core_relation: Self-RAG 13B improves ASQA citation precision over retrieval-augmented ChatGPT but lowers recall and correctness, so attribution gains do not establish better overall answering. Self-RAG 7B improves same-data PopQA accuracy. More support weighting costs MAUVE; less retrieval hurts PopQA more than PubHealth.
readings.scope: Same five ASQA passages: precision 70.3 versus 65.1, recall 71.3 versus 76.6, str-em 31.7 versus 40.7. PopQA accuracy: 54.9% versus 48.7%.
readings.witness: without isolating reflection from retrieval-aware training
readings.unclear: Reflection's isolated contribution is not recoverable.

readings.core_relation: Against a same-data baseline, Self-RAG 7B improves PopQA accuracy and ASQA citation precision but slightly lowers ASQA correctness. Against retrieval-augmented ChatGPT, 13B improves precision while lowering recall and correctness. Selective retrieval and critique therefore require task-specific output-quality priorities.
readings.scope: Baseline lacks training passages/reflection and receives test-time retrieval. ASQA uses identical five documents; stronger support weighting lowers MAUVE, and reduced retrieval harms PopQA more than PubHealth.
readings.witness: Its stronger precision does not establish broader evidence coverage

readings.core_relation: Reordering the answer passage within unchanged document sets isolates position sensitivity; adding distractors tests context-length effects. UUID retrieval limits semantic confounds, while repeating the query on both sides tests whether advance query access helps lookup and question answering.
readings.scope: 2,655 NaturalQuestions-Open queries; Contriever Wikipedia distractors exclude annotated answers; 10/20/30 documents. UUID sizes: 75/140/300, 500 examples each. Greedy-decoded outputs are scored by answer inclusion; no-document and answer-only references.
readings.witness: tests position without changing which passage supplies the answer

readings.core_relation: Self-RAG trains retrieval decisions and evidence judgments alongside text, then selects passage-conditioned sentences using predicted support, relevance, and generation scores. Offline critic supervision replaces separate inference-time evaluation, making attribution-versus-quality tradeoffs adjustable without retraining.
readings.scope: Zero-shot 7B/13B evaluation across six tasks; 7B PopQA accuracy rises from 48.7% to 54.9% over a same-data baseline. ASQA 13B precision improves but recall/correctness decline; stronger support weighting lowers MAUVE.
readings.witness: trade-offs between attribution and other aspects of answer quality

readings.core_relation: A GPT-4-supervised critic annotates retrieval and critique tokens offline; next-token training teaches the generator to produce them. At inference, a retrieval-probability threshold requests passages, and beam search combines generation scores with normalized critique probabilities to select candidate sentences. Predicted support thus affects claim selection without an inference-time critic.
readings.scope: Llama 2-7B critic; retrieved passages are masked from training loss. Support weights and retrieval thresholds are adjustable without retraining.

readings.core_relation: Moving an answer passage while fixing questions and available documents tests position-dependent evidence use; changing distractor counts tests added context without changing the answer. Closed-book and answer-only controls separate evidence availability from distractor competition; UUID lookup reduces linguistic confounds, and query repetition probes advance query contextualization.
readings.scope: 2,655 NaturalQuestions-Open queries with paragraph long answers; 10/20/30 documents; distractors exclude annotated answers. Greedy decoding is evaluated by correct-answer/value inclusion.
readings.witness: holding the question and available documents fixed

readings.core_relation: SELF-RAG learns retrieval decisions and evidence evaluations through offline critic annotations, then ranks passage-conditioned continuations by generation probabilities and self-evaluations. Support thereby influences output selection, with retrieval/support adjustment possible without retraining, but citation improvements come with correctness and fluency tradeoffs.
readings.scope: Zero-shot Llama 2 7B/13B on six tasks; same-data ASQA 7B comparison uses identical five documents: precision 66.9% versus 5.0%, str-em 30.0% versus 31.0%. Higher support weighting reduces MAUVE.
readings.witness: a tradeoff rather than uniform improvement

readings.core_relation: Query repetition gives GPT-3.5-Turbo (16K) perfect UUID retrieval but leaves question-answering positional weaknesses, distinguishing lookup success from natural-language evidence use. Flan-UL2's middle-position disadvantage emerges beyond its training window; similar standard/16K profiles on shared-length inputs show that nominal capacity does not establish robust answering.
readings.scope: 300 UUID pairs: 100% versus worst-position 45.6%. Flan-UL2 has only a 1.9-point best-to-worst gap within 2,048 training tokens; repetition slightly helps first-document QA and hurts elsewhere.

readings.core_relation: Position-controlled question answering and synthetic lookup distinguish usable evidence from nominal context capacity. Middle-position QA degradation persists despite query repetition fixing lookup; larger supported windows and higher retrieval recall do not necessarily improve answering.
readings.scope: Evaluated systems only; some document-rich configurations underperform closed-book answering. Extended/short-context counterparts behave similarly when both fit inputs; encoder-decoder models are relatively position-insensitive within training lengths, degrading beyond them. Reader accuracy saturates before retrieval recall.
readings.witness: rather than nominal context capacity or evidence availability alone

readings.core_relation: Changing evidence position and distractor count shows that context capacity and exact retrieval do not guarantee usable answer evidence. Question answering generally favors context ends over the middle; query repetition nearly perfects lookup without correcting that answering pattern.
readings.scope: 2,655 NaturalQuestions-Open queries plus random key-value lookup; tested models only. GPT-3.5-Turbo sometimes underperforms closed-book answering; standard/extended variants perform similarly on shared-fitting inputs; Claude-1.3 variants achieve nearly perfect synthetic retrieval.
readings.witness: not how consistently it uses the evidence provided

readings.core_relation: GPT-3.5-Turbo can fall below closed-book accuracy despite an answer passage remaining present, showing ineffective evidence use rather than unavailable information. Standard/16K variants share positional weaknesses on jointly fitting inputs; query repetition fixes UUID lookup but largely preserves question-answering weakness.
readings.scope: Answer-only accuracy: 88.3%; worst 20/30-document configurations below 56.1%. Shared-window comparison uses 10/20 documents. With 300 key-value pairs, 16K retrieval rises from worst-case 45.6% to perfect; QA declines slightly except with first-position evidence.

readings.core_relation: Offline critic labels teach the generator evidence judgments alongside text. At inference, segment-level beam search combines generation probability with normalized favorable relevance, support, and utility probabilities to rank passage-conditioned sentences; a normalized retrieval-probability threshold controls evidence requests. Learned assessments become adjustable selection criteria without retraining or an inference-time critic.
readings.scope: Llama 2 critic trained on GPT-4 reflection labels; passage tokens are excluded from loss; utility is passage-independent; support weights can change selected continuations.
readings.witness: rather than simply accepting the top retrieved passage
